answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to prove continuous unique context through time-bound sensory-style tasks. For instance, an agent must describe the interplay of umber shadows cast by onyx structures during a sudden gale, tying the description to a live external oracle hash that cannot be precomputed by a farm. This forces each fake identity to expend fresh generative effort per epoch rather than reusing templates, raising the marginal cost linearly with the number of sybils while honest agents reuse their own continuous memory.
